text: I inherited honesty and self-discipline from my father; from my mother, I inherited faith in goodness and deep kindness as did my three brothers and sisters.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: I wonder why some people tend to see science as something which takes man away from God. As I look at it, the path of science can always wind through the heart. For me, science has always been the path to spiritual enrichment and self-realisation.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: … the best way to win was to not need to win. The best performances are accomplished when you are relaxed and free of doubt.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: My impression of the American people can be summarized by a quotation from Benjamin Franklin, "Those things that hurt instruct!" I realised that people in this part of the world meet their problems head on. They attempt to get out of them rather than suffer them.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: I have always considered the price of perfection prohibitive and allowed mistakes as a part of the learning process. I prefer a dash of daring and persistence to perfection. I have always supported learning on the part of my team members by paying vigilant attention to each of their attempts, be they successful or unsuccessful.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: I was (and am) a terrible conversationist but consider myself a good communicator.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: To succeed in your mission, you must have single-minded devotion to your goal. Individuals like myself are often called 'workaholics'. I question this term because that implies a pathological condition or an illness. If I do what I desire more than anything else in the world and which makes me happy, such work can never be an aberration.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Total commitment is the common denominator among all successful men and women.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Climbing to the top demands strength, whether to the top of Mount Everest or to the top of your career.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Man needs his difficulties because they are necessary to enjoy success.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: To me, the level of responsibility is measured by one's ability to confront the decision-making process without any delay or distraction.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Happiness, satisfaction, and success in life depend on making the right choices, the winning choices. There are forces in life working for you and against you. One must distinguish the beneficial forces from the malevolent ones and choose correctly between them.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: You have to dream before your dreams can come true.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Perhaps the main motive behind my isolation was my desire to escape from the demands of relationships, which I consider very difficult in comparison to making rockets. All I desired was to be true to my way of life, to uphold the science of rocketry in my country and to retire with a clean conscience.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: It has been my personal experience that the true flavour, the real fun, the continuous excitement of work lie in the process of doing it rather than in having it over and done with.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: A person with belief never grovels before anyone, whining and whimpering that it's all too much, that he lacks support, that he is being treated unfairly. Instead, such a person tackes problems head on and then affirms, 'As a child of God, I am greater than anything that can happen to me.'
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: I never used any outside influence to advance my career. All I had was the inner urge to seek more within myself. The key to my motivation has always been to look at how far I had still to go rather than how far I had come.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: This is my belief: that through difficulties and problems God gives us the opportunity to grow. So when your hopes and dreams and goals are dashed, search among the wreckage, you may find a golden opportunity hidden in the ruins.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Great dreams of great dreamers are always transcended.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: I will not be presumptuous enough to say that my life can be a role model for anybody; but some poor child living in an obscure place in an underprivileged social setting may find a little solace in the way my destiny has been shaped. It could perhaps help such children liberate themselves from the bondage of their illusory backwardness and hopelessness.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Life is a difficult game. You can win it only by retaining your birthright to be a person. And to retain this right, you will have to be willing to take the social or external risks involved in ignoring pressures to do things the way others say they should be done.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Dream is not that which you see while sleeping; it is something that does not let you sleep.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: Source: *Wings of Fire: An Autobiography*, A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: If we are not free, no one will respect us.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: We must think and act like a nation of a billion people and not like that of a million people. Dream, dream, dream!
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: We have not invaded anyone. We have not conquered anyone. We have not grabbed their land, their culture, their history and tried to enforce our way of life on them.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: This will be the greatest legacy that we can proudly leave behind for our next generation, let us sacrifice our today so that our children can have a better tomorrow.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: No religion has mandated killing others as a requirement for its sustenance or promotion.
author: Abdul Kalam
label: Abdul Kalam

text: He who has a thousand friends has not a friend to spare, while he who has one enemy will meet him everywhere.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: The best companion and helper is admirable morals.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Two things cause people to be destroyed: fear of poverty and seeking superiority through pride.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Submission to Allah's Will is the best companion; wisdom is the noblest heritage; theoretical and practical knowledge are the best signs of distinction; deep thinking will present the clearest picture of every problem.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: The mind of a wise man is the safest custody of secrets; cheerfulness is the key to friendship; patience and forbearance will conceal many defects.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: A conceited and self-admiring person is disliked by others; charity and alms are the best remedy for ailments and calamities; one has to account in the next world for the deeds that he has done in this world.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: If you overpower your enemy, then pardon him by way of thankfulness to Allah, for being able to subdue him.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Unfortunate is he who cannot gain a few sincere friends during his life and more unfortunate is the one who has gained them and then lost them (through his deeds).
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: When some blessings come to you, do not drive them away through thanklessness.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: He who is deserted by friends and relatives will often find help and sympathy from strangers.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: One who rushes madly after inordinate desire, runs the risk of encountering destruction and death.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Often your utterances and expressions of your face leak out the secrets of your hidden thoughts.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Hearts of people are like wild beasts. They attach themselves to those who love and train them.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: So long as fortune is favouring you, your defects will remain covered.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Only he who has the power to punish can pardon.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Generosity is to help a deserving person without his request, and if you help him after his request, then it is either out of self-respect or to avoid rebuke.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: There is no greater wealth than wisdom, no greater poverty than ignorance; no greater heritage than culture and no greater support than consultation.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Patience is of two kinds: patience over what pains you, and patience against what you covet.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Wealth converts a strange land into homeland and poverty turns a native place into a strange land.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Contentment is the capital which will never diminish.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Wealth is the fountain head of passions.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Whoever warns you against sins and vices is like the one who gives you good tidings.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Tongue is a beast, if it is let loose, it devours.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: O son of Adam, when you see that your Lord, the Glorified, bestows His Favors on you while you disobey Him, you should fear Him (take warning that His Wrath may not turn those very blessings into misfortunes).
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: A virtuous person is better than virtue and a vicious person is worse than vice.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Recommended prayers cannot attain the pleasures of Allah for you when obligatory prayers are left unattended.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Value of a man depends upon his courage; his veracity depends upon his self-respect and his chastity depends upon his sense of honor.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Every breath you take is a step towards death.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Like your body your mind also gets tired so refresh it by wise sayings.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Whenever a tradition of the Holy Prophet is related to you, scrutinize it, do not be satisfied with mere verbatim repetition of the same because there are many people who repeat the words containing knowledge but only few ponder over them and try to fully grasp the meaning they convey.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Anyone who loves us Ahlul Bayt must be ready to face a life of austerity.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: A friend cannot be considered a friend unless he is tested on three occasions: in time of need, behind your back and after your death.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: There is enough light for one who wants to see.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: It is wiser to abstain than to repent.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Obstinacy will prevent you from a correct decision.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: If two opposite theories are propagated one will be wrong.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: When truth was revealed to me I never doubted it.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Death is never very far.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: One who forsakes truth earns eternal damnation.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: O son of Adam, if you have collected anything in excess of your actual need, you will act only as its trustee for someone else to use it.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: There are people who worship Allah to gain His Favors, this is the worship of traders; while there are some who worship Him to keep themselves free from His Wrath, this is the worship of slaves; a few who obey Him out' of their sense of gratitude and obligations, this is the worship of free and noble men.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Where are those who protect honour, and those self-respecting persons who defend respectable persons in the time of hardship? Shame is behind you while Paradise is in front of you.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: During civil disturbance adopt such an attitude that people do not attach any importance to you — they neither burden you with complicated affairs, nor try to derive any advantage out of you.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: When Imam Ali was asked about Faith in Religion, he replied that the structure of faith is supported by four pillars endurance, conviction, justice and jihad.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: To refrain from unlawful and impious source of pleasures is an ornament to the poor and to be thankful for the riches granted is the adornment of wealth.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: If you cannot get things as much as you desire than be contented with what you have.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: An ignorant person will always overdo a thing or neglect it totally.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: The wiser a man is, the less talkative will he be.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Time wears out bodies, renews hopes, brings death nearer and takes away aspirations. Whoever gets anything from the world lives in anxiety for holding it and whoever loses anything passes his days grieving over the loss.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Whoever wants to be a leader should educate himself before educating others. Before preaching to others he should first practice himself. Whoever educates himself and improves his own morals is superior to the man who tries to teach and train others.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Anything which can be counted is finite and will come to an end.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: If matters get mixed up then scrutinize the cause and you will know what the effects will be.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: A man sarcastically started praising Imam Ali, though he had no faith in him and Imam Ali hearing these praises from him said "I am less than what you tell about me but more than what you think about me."
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Those who have come alive out of a blood-bath live longer and have more children.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: One who imagines himself to be all-knowing will surely suffer on account of his ignorance.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: I appreciate an old man's cautious opinion more than the valor of a young man.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: I wonder at a man who loses hope of salvation when the door of repentance is open for him.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Nawf bin Fizala Bakali, the famous scholar of the early Islamic days says that one night he was with Imam Ali. In the middle of the night, Imam Ali got up from his bed, looked for sometime at the stars and inquired of Nawf whether he was awake. Nawf said: "I got from my bed replying, "Yes, Amirul Mo'minin (Commander of the Faithful) ! I am awake".
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Imam Ali said Nawf! Those are the fortunate people who adopt piety as the principle of their lives and are fully attentive to their welfare for the Hereafter. They accept bare earth as the most comfortable bed and water as the most pleasant drink. They adopt the Holy Qur'an and prayers as their guide and protector and like Prophet Jesus Christ (Isa) they forsake the world and its vicious pleasure.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Nawf! Prophet David (Daud) once got up at such an hour in the night and said this was the hour when prayers of everyone who prayed were accepted except of those who forcibly collected revenues or who were scandal- mongers or were persons in the police force of a despotic regime or were musicians".
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: If you understand Allah's Majesty, then you will not attach any importance to the creatures.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: If you want to pray to Allah for better means of subsistence, then first give something in charity
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: When someone is sure of the returns, then he shows generosity.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Aid (from Allah) is in proportion to the trouble.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: He who practices moderation and frugality will never be threatened with poverty.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: One of the conveniences in life is to have less children.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Loving one another is half of wisdom.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Grief is half of old age.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Grant of patience (from Allah) is in proportion to the extent of calamity you are passing through. If you exhibit fretfulness, irritation, and despair in calamities, then your patience and your exertions are wasted.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Many persons get nothing out of their fasts but hunger and thirst, many more get nothing out of their night prayers but exertions and sleepless nights. Wise and sagacious persons are praiseworthy even if they do not fast and sleep during the nights.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Defend your faith (in Allah) with the help of charity. Protect your wealth with the aid of Zakat. Let the prayers guard you from calamities and disasters.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: The first fruit of forbearance is that people will sympathize with you and they will go against the man who offended you arrogantly.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: One who takes account of his shortcomings will always gain by it; one who is unmindful of them will always suffer. One who is afraid of the Day of Judgment, is safe from the Wrath of Allah. One who takes lessons from the events of life, gets vision, one who acquires vision becomes wise and one who attains wisdom achieves knowledge.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Bear sorrows and calamities patiently, otherwise you will never be happy.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: One who comes into power often oppresses.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Adversities often bring good qualities to the front.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: If a friend envies you, then he is not a true friend.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Avarice dulls the faculties of judgment and wisdom.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Oppression and tyranny are the worse companions for the Hereafter.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: The best deed of a great man is to forgive and forget.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Silence will create respect and dignity; justice and fairplay will bring more friends; benevolence and charity will enhance prestige and position; courtesy will draw benevolence; service of mankind will secure leadership and good words will overcome powerful enemies.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: A greedy man will always find himself in the shackles of humility.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: These are the orders issued by the creature of Allah, Ali, the son Abu Taalib to Maalik, the son of Ashtar when he appointed Maalik as the Governor of Egypt to collect zakat there, to combat the enemies of Islam and Egypt, to work for the welfare of its people and to look after its prosperity.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Do not feel ashamed to forgive and forget.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Do not hurry over punishments and do not be pleased and do not be proud of your power to punish.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Do not get angry and lose your temper quickly over the mistakes and failures of those over whom you rule. On the contrary, be patient and sympathetic with them.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Never say to yourself, "I am their Lord, their ruler and all in all over them and that I must be obeyed submissively and humbly" because such a thought will unbalance your mind, will make you vain and arrogant, will weaken your faith in religion and will make you seek support of any power other than that of Allah.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Being ungrateful for a blessing causes it to be taken away.
author: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)
label: Ali ibn Abi Talib (R.A)

text: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said to Khalid ibn al-Walid: 'Strive for death, then you will be given life.'"واحرص على الموت توهب لك الحياة" Al-ʿIqd al-Farīd author Ibn Abd Rabbih (1/92 )
author: Abu Bakr (R.A)
label: Abu Bakr (R.A)

text: I know that you are just a stone and that you can neither do any harm nor give benefit. Had I not seen Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allâh be upon him) kissing you, I would not have kissed you.
author: Umar ibn Al-Khattāb (R.A)
label: Umar ibn Al-Khattāb (R.A)
